items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: If I was a second engineer working behind let’s say John Krause at Capitol

ctx.x: The first time I ever saw in the studio tape slicing and splicing I was amazed that it worked. I just didn’t know such a thing was done the first time I saw it. So do you recall the first time you ever did that and were you nervous about it?

You bet. But it didn’t happen very often. If I was a second engineer working behind let’s say John Krause at Capitol — I mean he would — in those days on a date, I’m talking about twenty years ago, the engineer could turn around and say, “Would you take the first half of the tune up through the first chorus and cut it to the next take of the same chorus.” You know and that happens on a date, when there’s twenty guys in the room talking. That’s when you can get in trouble, I mean as a second engineer. I as an…
Am I correct that you would manipulate the tape over the heads so that you would hear —
